title: Next-to-Leading-Order Electroweak Corrections to Quantum Observables in Lepton-Lepton Collisions
authors: Spencer Chang, Thomas Driscoll, Sokratis Trifinopoulos
abstract: We study how virtual next-to-leading-order electroweak corrections affect the quantum observables of entanglement and magic in lepton--lepton collisions. Treating the outgoing particles as multi-qudit systems, $\textit{i.e.}$, qubits for spin-$\tfrac{1}{2}$ fermions and qutrits for massive vector bosons, we compute entanglement entropy and the stabilizer second Rényi entropy for the processes $\ell^+\ell^- \to τ^-τ^+,\, ZZ$ at one-loop accuracy. We show that radiative corrections coherently modify the quantum structure of the final state, shifting regions of maximal entanglement and altering the generated magic relative to leading order. Our results demonstrate that these quantum observables provide novel, precision-sensitive probes of electroweak dynamics at future lepton colliders and open a path toward their use in searches for new physics.
summary: This paper calculates how electroweak radiative corrections affect quantum measures like entanglement and magic in processes such as $\ell^+\ell^- 	o 	au^-	au^+$ and $ZZ$. By treating the final state as a multi-qudit system, the authors show that these corrections coherently alter the quantum structure of the final state. The results establish these quantum observables as powerful, new tools for precision measurements at future lepton colliders.
main_problem: The study investigates how virtual next-to-leading-order (NLO) electroweak corrections modify the quantum structure of observables like entanglement and magic in lepton-lepton collisions.
main_result: Radiative corrections coherently modify the quantum structure of the final state, causing shifts in regions of maximal entanglement and altering the generated magic relative to leading order.
method: The authors compute entanglement entropy and stabilizer second Rényi entropy by treating outgoing particles as multi-qudit systems and performing one-loop calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is lepton-lepton collisions ($\ell^+\ell^- 	o 	au^-	au^+, ZZ$), analyzed within Quantum Field Theory. The outgoing particles are modeled as multi-qudit systems (qubits for fermions, qutrits for massive bosons).
key_observables: Entanglement entropy, stabilizer second Rényi entropy, and 'magic' (non-stabilizerness).
important_parameters: Next-to-leading-order (NLO) electroweak corrections, future lepton collider energies, and particle masses.
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on the production-side quantum state before decay reconstruction, and the initial state is assumed to have definite helicities.
paper_structure: The paper systematically calculates quantum observables by incorporating one-loop electroweak corrections, detailing the theoretical framework for handling divergences and projecting the state onto the outgoing two-particle Hilbert space.
why_interesting: The application of quantum information diagnostics (entanglement, magic) to high-energy particle physics processes provides a novel, precision-sensitive probe of fundamental interactions, bridging quantum information theory with particle phenomenology.
